title: Impacts of Braided River Morphodynamics and Damming on Habitat Quality for Schizothorax waltoni in the Lhasa River: Insights From Ecohydraulic Modelling
content:
ABSTRACT

Braided rivers are complex ecosystems that foster a rich diversity of species through their unique topography, flow variability, and sediment transport. However, dam construction and land use change, including hydromorphological alterations, are problematic for braided rivers. This study investigates the impacts of braided river morphodynamics and damming on the habitat of Schizothorax waltoni Regan, 1905 (S. waltoni) in the Lhasa River, China, using ecohydraulic modelling built in Telemac 2D open software. Our findings revealed that adult S. waltoni adapted well to varying flow conditions, with habitat suitability index (HSP) values ranging from 5% at 50 m3/s to 56% at 4000 m3/s. In contrast, spawning habitats showed lower HSP values, indicating vulnerability. The study highlighted that damming primarily negatively affected fry habitats in upstream areas while benefiting juvenile and adult fish habitats. These results emphasize the need for water resource management that considers ecological impacts. Sustainable practices in the Lhasa River basin are crucial for conservation, and the insights gained can inform similar efforts in other river systems. Decision makers should integrate these findings to ensure the sustainable management of river ecosystems and their resident species.
